title: Items common to both lists
description: Write a function `common_items(a, b)` that returns a sorted list of the values present in both list `a` and list `b`.
hints: Sets have an operation that directly gives you the elements shared between two collections.
Converting both lists to sets lets you use the `&` operator (set intersection) to find common values.
Build `set(a) & set(b)` to get the intersection of the two lists, then return `sorted(...)` of that result.
expected_behavior: Returns a sorted list of the distinct values that appear in both `a` and `b`.
solution:
def common_items(a, b):
    return sorted(set(a) & set(b))
explanation: Converting both lists to sets and combining them with the `&` operator computes their intersection, i.e. the values present in both. `sorted()` then turns that intersection into a deterministic, ascending list.
